title: Multivariate Analysis of Variegated Expression in Neurons
author: Hannah M Shoenhard
materials: Permeabilize larvae Thaw trypsin 0.05% Trypsin -EDTA on ice. Trypsin-EDTA 0.05% phenol red Gibco - Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #25300054

Dilute antibodies 1:200 for anti-GFP and 1:500 for anti-tERK in 1%BSA, 1%DMSO in PBS-T chicken anti-GFP ROCKLAND antibodes & assays Catalog #600-901-B12 anti-tERK Cell Signaling Technology Catalog #4696 Note: this protocol should hypothetically work with any tagged expression construct, not just GFP-tagged constructs. Substitute antibodies as appropriate in order to visualize your expression construct. Remove blocking solution from larvae and apply primary-- I use 1000 uL of primary in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for 50-100 larvae, but less can be used if necessary as long as the larvae remain completely submerged in primary while incubating overnight.

We used Goat anti-Mouse IgG1 Cross-Adsorbed Secondary Antibody Alexa Fluor™ 633 Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #A-21126 (RRID: AB_2535768) to label tERK in red and Alexa Fluor® 488 AffiniPure Donkey Anti-Chicken IgY (IgG) (H L) Jackson ImmunoResearch Laboratories, Inc. Catalog #703-545-155 to label GFP. Dilute both antibodies 1:500 in 1% BSA, 1% DMSO in PBS-T, taking care not to expose to light.
Split channels using Colors🡪 Split channels

steps.title: Perform Mating Cross
steps.instruction: Perform the mating cross for the experiment (e.g., Gal4 x UAS-induced rescue of loss-of-function phenotype).

substeps.instruction: Cross fish heterozygous or homozygous mutant for the gene of interest.
Ensure at least one fish carries a Gal4 for the cell type of interest and one carries a UAS construct expressing a tagged version of the target gene.
Keep larvae from different mating crosses separate during raising, behavior, and analysis.

steps.title: Assay and Sort Phenotypes
steps.instruction: Assay the phenotype of interest in larvae, preferably at 6 dpf (5 dpf is also acceptable).

substeps.instruction: Sort larvae according to phenotype and keep different phenotypes separate.
Define phenotypic groups based on the spectrum of behavior (e.g., collecting extreme ends of the spectrum).

steps.title: Label Larvae
steps.instruction: Physically label larvae so phenotypes are clearly identifiable (e.g., blunt vs. angled tail cuts, removing pectoral fins).

steps.title: Optional Methanol Storage
steps.instruction: If needed, store larvae in individual wells in 100% methanol for 1-2 days after phenotyping but before fixation. Ensure larvae do not dry out.

steps.title: Fix Larvae
steps.instruction: Fix larvae in 4% PFA in PBS + 0.25% Triton (PBS-T) overnight at 4°C.

substeps.instruction: Use room-temperature PFA and fix at RT for 5-10 minutes before moving to 4°C.
Wash off PFA with three 5-minute PBS-T washes.

steps.title: Post-Fixation Storage
steps.instruction: Store larvae for 1-2 weeks at 4°C in PBS (not PBS-T) or proceed immediately to immunostaining.

steps.title: Bleach Larvae
steps.instruction: Bleach pigment cells (skip if larvae were raised in PTU).

substeps.instruction: Prepare fresh bleaching solution: combine 700 uL PBS-T, 200 uL 5% KOH, and 100 uL 30% H2O2 (Merck MilliporeSigma #H1009-500ML) for a total of 1 mL.
Incubate on a rocker at RT for ~10 minutes or at 55°C for ~5 minutes until eyes are light orange.
Rinse immediately with 2-3 quick PBS-T washes, followed by one 5-minute PBS-T wash.

steps.title: Antigen Retrieval
steps.instruction: Perform antigen retrieval to ensure proper tERK signal.

substeps.instruction: Incubate in 150mM TrisHCl (pH 9) for 5 minutes at RT.
Transfer to 70°C water bath for 15 minutes.
Wash with PBS-T: one quick rinse, then two 5-minute washes.

steps.title: Trypsin Treatment
steps.instruction: Incubate 6 dpf larvae in trypsin on ice for 45 minutes (10 minutes may be sufficient for 5-6 dpf larvae).

substeps.instruction: Rinse trypsin off with two quick PBS-T washes until all pink is gone.
Wash for 10 minutes with PBS-T.

steps.title: Block Larvae
steps.instruction: Block larvae using a solution made in PBS-T containing 2% Normal Goat Serum (NGS), 1% BSA, and 1% DMSO.

steps.title: Apply Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Apply primary antibody in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube using ~1 mL of blocking solution.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 1 hour on a rocker at room temperature.
Incubate overnight on a gentle rocker or rotator at 4°C.
Wash off primary antibody with three 15-minute washes in PBS-T on a rocker at room temperature.

steps.title: Apply Secondary Antibody
steps.instruction: Apply secondary antibody and incubate overnight in the dark (e.g., using an opaque box or aluminum foil) on a gentle rocker or rotator at 4°C.

substeps.instruction: Wash off secondary antibody in the dark with three 15-minute washes in PBS-T on a rocker at room temperature.

steps.title: Store and Mount Larvae
steps.instruction: Store larvae at 4°C in total darkness in a 2:1 mixture of VECTASHIELD Mounting Medium (Vector Laboratories #H-1000) and PBS for at least overnight or up to 2 weeks.

substeps.instruction: Mount Vectashield-soaked larvae in 1.1%-1.25% low-melt agarose in a glass-bottomed petri dish, dorsal side down.
Ensure larvae are mounted with no tilt (left-to-right or front-to-back).

steps.title: Image Brains
steps.instruction: Image brains using a confocal microscope (e.g., Zeiss 880 with 20X 0.8 NA air lens at 0.8 zoom).

substeps.instruction: Use the 'tile' function to capture and stitch images of the forebrain, midbrain, rostral hindbrain, caudal hindbrain, and anterior spinal cord.
Set step size to 2 microns; a brain typically comprises 130-150 slices.
Calibrate laser intensity and gain so the brightest neurons are saturated.
Save images in 8-bit format.

steps.title: Post-Imaging Processing
steps.instruction: Process larvae after imaging.

substeps.instruction: Place each individually-identified larva in a well of a genotyping plate.
Genotype larvae according to specific protocol (e.g., Zhang et al 2020 for live larvae).

steps.title: Prepare Images in FIJI
steps.instruction: Prepare images for registration using FIJI (ImageJ).

substeps.instruction: Orient brains exactly vertically using Transform -> Rotate.
If imaged dorsal side closest to coverslip, flip Z orientation using Transform -> Flip Z.
Save individual channels as .nrrd files: suffix _01 for tERK and _02 for GFP/marker.

steps.title: Register Brains to Reference
steps.instruction: Register brains using CMTK Registration Runner GUI in FIJI/MobaXterm.

substeps.instruction: Download the reference brain from ZBrain 2.0 atlas.
Set CMTK library to Fiji.app/lib/cmtk_munger_wsl_linux.

Set registration parameters: Affine transformation (checked), Warp transformation (checked), Channels for registration (checked), Reformat (checked), Threads (auto), Exploration (52), Coarsest (8), Refine (3), Grid spacing (80), Accuracy (1.0).
Run registration and verify tERK channel against reference brain.

steps.title: Smooth and Reformat Stacks
steps.instruction: Process registered GFP channels (_02) using the PrepareStacksForMAPMapping.ijm macro in FIJI.

substeps.instruction: Set maximum pixel intensity to 256 for 8-bit images.
Run macro to generate .tiff files.

steps.title: Quantify Signal in Matlab
steps.instruction: Quantify GFP signal using the QuantifySignalMultipleBrains.m function in Matlab.

substeps.instruction: Provide the folder containing .tiff files and the files 'AnatomyLabelDatabaseDownsampled.hdf5' and 'MaskDatabaseDownsampled.mat'.
Input metadata for each brain during the loop to generate a .csv file containing signal intensity for 293 brain regions.

steps.title: Perform Multivariate Analysis in R
steps.instruction: Analyze the quantified data using RStudio.

substeps.instruction: Install required packages: tidyverse, glmnet, readxl, janitor, hablar, ggpubr, here, gt, ComplexHeatmap, circlize, corrplot, renv.
Load custom functions: export_top_PC_regions.R, exportStrongestCorrelatedRegions.R, filterCaudalBrain.R, graph_PC_components.R, normalizeSignalBy.R, tidyImportedDataUnderscore.R.
Use tidyImportedDataUnderscore.R to transpose and split the FishName column into metadata columns (FishNum, pair, geno, pheno, collected, Imaged).
Load the 293_BrainRegions_Translator.xlsx for region abbreviations.
Perform correlational analysis to identify regions highly correlated with a target region (e.g., DCR6).
